options.content: Every successful `/predict` call writes one row to the database -- this dashboard reads those rows directly (not log files). It answers "what is the model being asked, and how is it answering" -- not whether those answers are *correct* (see the **Drift** dashboard for the closest proxy to that). Use the time range picker (top right) to zoom into any window -- every panel below respects it.

panels.title: Sentiment split
panels.description: Share of positive vs negative predictions in the selected time range. A sudden big swing (e.g. normally ~50/50, suddenly 95% negative) is worth checking -- either real-world sentiment genuinely shifted, or something about incoming traffic changed (see the Drift dashboard).

targets.rawSql: SELECT sentiment, count(*) AS value FROM predictions WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at) GROUP BY sentiment

panels.title: Confidence distribution
panels.description: How confident the model was in whatever it predicted (0.5 = a coin flip, 1.0 = fully confident), for the selected time range. Most of this should sit well above 0.5 -- a distribution drifting down toward 0.5 over time usually also shows up as a rising "prediction confidence" PSI on the Drift dashboard.

panels.title: Predictions per minute
panels.description: Request volume over time -- how many reviews were scored per minute in the selected range. Useful for correlating a drift alert or a latency spike with an actual change in traffic.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('minute', received_at) AS time, count(*) AS value FROM predictions WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
